name: three-body
desc: 三体编程语言 Three Body Language written in Rust
why: An esoteric programming language inspired by the Three-Body Problem, written in Rust, with a delightfully odd premise.

brief.what_it_is: Three Body Language (三体编程语言) is an esoteric programming language written in Rust, with keywords and built-in function names taken from Liu Cixin's Three-Body Problem novels. You write a source file or type into a REPL and run it with the 3body binary, which interprets the code. Variables are bound with 给 and 以, functions with 法则, loops with 面壁, and output is printed with 广播. The README says the language is still at a 'concept level'.
brief.why_it_exists: The README does not state a purpose beyond being a fun language themed on the Three-Body Problem. Its own framing is that it is 'still a concept-level programming language' (仍然是一个概念级的编程语言), with features like 面壁, 破壁, 思想钢印 and 冬眠 already implemented.
brief.how_it_works: The interpreter follows the design of Thorsten Ball's book Writing An Interpreter In Go, and the README credits wadackel/rs-monkey-lang and flaneur2020/pua-lang as inspiration, plus Monkey-Rust-2021-Edition. Threads are created through a 程心 object with cx.thread(...) and joined with cx.join(...). The README gives no deeper detail on the internals.

brief.install_notes: The README lists only brew install three-body. Building from source needs a Rust toolchain with cargo, and the REPL needs the 'repl' cargo feature. No accounts, hardware or extra config are mentioned. The repo links a separate VS Code extension (3body-vscode-language-server) on the Visual Studio Marketplace.
brief.standout: The language is a full keyword remap of an interpreter from a Go book into Chinese, and its keywords are Three-Body Problem lines: 思想钢印 for constants, 面壁 for while loops, 破壁 for break, 冬眠 for sleep, and 没关系的都一样 for deep equality. The threads are named after characters and companies from the novels, for example 程心 and 星环公司.
brief.status: unknown. The README has CI, crates.io and Homebrew badges, a GitHub Actions run link, and a VS Code extension, but no release date, version or changelog in the text I read. I did not check the commit history or releases page, so I cannot say whether it is maintained.
brief.caveats: The README calls it a concept-level language, so expect an early project with limited features. Its own syntax table lists 二向箔清理 (clear) and 毁灭 (exit), but the README shows no examples of them, so do not assume they work. The entry is written in Chinese with English gloss, so the README's English is partial. The threading examples are shown with a CI run link, not a standalone demo. License is MIT.
